title: Endocrine System Anatomy: Pituitary, Adrenal & Thyroids
description: Discover endocrine system anatomy across the hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroids, adrenals, pancreatic islets, and gonadal hormone axes.
h1: Endocrine System Anatomy: Hypothalamus, Pituitary and Hormone Glands
blurb: Hormone-secreting glands—hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroids, adrenals, pancreas, and gonads—communicating through bloodstream feedback loops.
lead: Unlike exocrine glands that empty into ducts, endocrine glands release chemical messengers directly into surrounding capillaries to coordinate metabolism, growth, and stress responses. In this illustrated guide to endocrine system anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including pituitary gland, pineal gland, thyroid gland, parathyroid glands—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Unlike exocrine glands that empty into ducts, endocrine glands release chemical messengers directly into surrounding capillaries to coordinate metabolism, growth, and stress responses. Every ductless gland on one figure — including the ones you never see: pineal, parathyroids, adrenals and the islets. Within the human body, the endocrine system (Systema endocrinum) is situated in whole body — ductless glands, receives arterial perfusion via rich arterial supply to each gland, and is innervated by autonomic + trophic hormones.

Structurally, the pituitary gland (Hypophysis) comprises pea-sized master gland in the sella turcica. Physiologically, the pituitary gland releases ACTH, TSH, GH, LH/FSH, prolactin, ADH/oxytocin store. The pineal gland (Glandula pinealis) is tiny cone on the dorsal diencephalon. Physiologically, the pineal gland governs melatonin — circadian rhythm. Structurally, the thyroid gland (Glandula thyroidea) comprises butterfly gland on the trachea. Physiologically, the thyroid gland governs t3/T4 metabolic rate; calcitonin. The parathyroid glands (Gll. parathyroideae) are four grains on the thyroid's back. Physiologically, the parathyroid glands governs PTH — raises plasma calcium. Structurally, the adrenal glands (Gll. suprarenales) comprises caps on each kidney: cortex + medulla. Physiologically, the adrenal glands governs cortisol, aldosterone, adrenaline. Structurally, the pancreatic islets (Insulae pancreaticae) comprises 1–2 million islets in the pancreas. Physiologically, the pancreatic islets governs insulin (β) and glucagon (α) — glucose control.

Clinically, regarding the pituitary gland, pituitary adenoma → visual field loss (optic chiasm above). From a diagnostic standpoint, in the pineal gland, calcifies with age; useful midline marker on CT. In clinical pathology involving the thyroid gland, goitre and thyrotoxicosis are common presentations. Medical evaluation of the parathyroid glands also notes that accidental removal in thyroidectomy → tetany.

questions.question: What organs make up the endocrine system?
questions.answer: The endocrine system includes hormone-producing structures such as the pituitary, thyroid, parathyroids, adrenals and pancreatic islets, with other organs also contributing hormones. Structurally, the pancreatic beta cells comprises insulin-producing cells of endocrine pancreatic islets. Physiologically, the pancreatic beta cells lower circulating glucose by promoting uptake/storage.

questions.question: How do endocrine glands differ from exocrine glands?
questions.answer: Endocrine tissue releases hormones into the blood. Exocrine glands deliver products through ducts to a surface or lumen, as pancreatic acini do for digestion. The parathyroid chief cells is small endocrine cells of parathyroid glands. Physiologically, the parathyroid chief cells secrete PTH in response to falling ionized calcium.

questions.question: What is the pituitary gland?
questions.answer: Pea-sized master gland in the sella turcica. Functionally, it releases ACTH, TSH, GH, LH/FSH, prolactin, ADH/oxytocin store. In clinical pathology involving the pituitary gland, pituitary adenoma → visual field loss (optic chiasm above).

questions.question: Where in the neck is the thyroid gland located?
questions.answer: Butterfly gland on the trachea. Functionally, it governs t3/T4 metabolic rate; calcitonin. Medical evaluation of the thyroid gland also notes that goitre and thyrotoxicosis are common presentations.

questions.question: What is the function of the adrenal glands?
questions.answer: Functionally, it governs cortisol, aldosterone, adrenaline. Caps on each kidney: cortex + medulla. Clinically, regarding the adrenal glands, addison's: hypotension, pigmentation, fatigue.
